title: The effect of self-reflection on the outcomes of online clinical skills training: a comparative study
reason: RCT comparing an online module with vs without self-reflection prompts on knowledge, self-efficacy and observed skills. Only group contrasts; written reflections are not analysed against any outcome, so no indicator enters an analysis.

extraction.n_quote: resulting in a final sample of 88 participants (Control: N = 44; Experimental: N = 44)
extraction.population: undergraduate and postgraduate health and social science students, 1 university
extraction.lms_indicators: none analysed (asynchronous online module; experimental group's written reflections collected but not used as a measure)
extraction.outcome_or_construct: knowledge quiz, self-efficacy/confidence (self-report), observed consultation skills (checklist)
extraction.notes: Reported effects (e.g. Cohen's d = 0.46, 0.59) are condition effects (group membership), not indicator-outcome relations, so not extracted. Online module delivered via recorded lecture and Qualtrics, not an LMS.
